 Most recent Most popular Jaissle 'tried his best' to keep Guimaraes published at 17:28 GMT 17:28 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle says he "tried his best" to keep Bruno Guimaraes at the club as the Brazilian returns to St James' Park for the first time in an Arsenal shirt. 
 Media caption, 'I tried my best' - Jaissle on attempt to keep Guimaraes
 1 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:27 GMT 17:27 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 The teams are out at St James' Park and we're moments away from kick-off. 
 Chance for Arsenal to move eight clear at the summit with a win. 
 18 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'One step forward' published at 17:26 GMT 17:26 GMT 
 FT: Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, speaking to Sky Sports: "A little bit frustrated but how we are building our team and recovering our confidence in our style of playing, today was a step forward.
 "We were dominating, we were progressing with passes and we were in a good position to control the game but we didn't create many clear chances. 
 "But this is the way and the idea we have to try and implement. Today we avoided the moment of them dominating us and avoiding giving up chances to the opponent. We did a lot of things good. 
 "Today is not enough but we know how we have to try and build the team and how we can feel better. One step forward clear in the style. Keep going forward."
 4 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Williams-Barnett is 'just unbelievable' published at 17:23 GMT 17:23 GMT 
 FT: Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham defender Destiny Udogie to BBC Match of the Day: "We are finding the right connection between us and the manager. We are all working towards the same goal.
 "His [Roberto de Zerbi's] style of play. Also we are fighting for each other on the pitch for 90 minutes and I think that was something that was missing at the start but we have found it now.
 "New players coming in and a new manager with a different style of play, it always takes some time but we are finding the connection between us."
 On Luca Williams-Barnett's performance: "Obviously I am so happy for him, every day in the training session he shows his quality. Honestly he's just an incredible football player. I hope he keeps doing what he's doing.
 "Obviously he is such a young lad. Doing what he is doing in training and in the game is just unbelievable. I just wish him the best."

 Click 'Get Involved' to have your say 
 Emi Martinez had already lost a yard of pace, even before his broken jaw. Retirement beckons, but he does have a world cup winners medal to his name. Time to hang up his gloves.
 Rob, Huddersfield

 Arteta warns Arsenal players over FPL team news leak published at 17:19 GMT 17:19 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Mikel Arteta says his Arsenal players have been warned against inadvertently leaking team news via Fantasy Premier League.
 The intervention comes after Christos Tzolis selected and captained himself in his Fantasy Premier League (FPL) team before Arsenal 's match against Liverpool on 1 November, after he had missed a month through injury.
 The Gunners manager picked the winger in Arsenal 's starting XI at Anfield in what was his first appearance since Greece's Nations League draw with the Netherlands on 1 October.
 Before today's match at Newcastle , Arteta said he had to speak to his squad, and those close to the club, about their FPL selections.
 "With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," he said. "They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.
 "This is the kind of thing that is happening in our society right now. It's something new. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.
 "Obviously, confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and about what you are trying to do and that should be kept as a huge secret. We'll take measures to make sure it doesn't happen."

 'Evanilson is lovely' published at 17:18 GMT 17:18 GMT 
 FT: Bournemouth 2-0 Nottm Forest 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth striker Justin Kluivert: "Delighted, we are very proud. Especially after the international break, it is important to restart again and we did a brilliant job today.
 On strike partner Evanilson, who has scored in six straight league matches: "He is lovely, he works hard and his quality does the rest. I am happy he has been scoring, and working hard for the team.
 On going fourth: "We just stay humble and go game to game, we don't look too far ahead. We have the Europa League and then Fulham away, they played a good game today. We go for another win and do not settle for less."

 Jaissle needs a result published at 17:16 GMT 17:16 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 Today feels like a big game for Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.
 With just one win in five games, the Magpies need three points. 
 18 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Magpies' miserable record against league leaders published at 17:16 GMT 17:16 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 Newcastle have already lost a joint-high seven top-flight home games this calendar year and the omens suggest they may struggle against Arsenal. The Magpies have failed to score in 32 Premier League games against the Gunners - the most by a side against one opponent in the competition's history.
 Their record against elite teams also offers little encouragement. Newcastle have not beaten the reigning champions since a 2-1 win over Manchester City in 2019 and have just one victory from their past 29 Premier League games against sides starting the day top.
 Image source, Opta

 'A step in the right direction' published at 17:16 GMT 17:16 GMT 
 Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland 
 Steph Houghton 
Former England defender on Final Score 
 Villa Park is a tough place to go, for Sunderland to keep two clean sheets in the past two games is good. It's a step in the right direction. 
 22 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Really important to be solid' published at 17:16 GMT 17:16 GMT 
 FT: Aston Villa 0-0 Sunderland 
 Sunderland 
 Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris, speaking to BBC MOTD: "Being hard to beat was one of the main objectives today. It was really important to be solid and I think the lads showed a great mentality.
 "We had a few balls to exploit and even at the end with just a bit more maturity and more confidence it was possible to score a goal.
 "We showed today we are a really good team when we want to defend together.
 "I told them when you feel the opponents getting frustrated it is a good sign and it happened in the first half. A good point on the road.
 "The points are important, sometimes you play well and don't get anything. 
 "It is the strength of the squad, the mindset and stability. I am really proud of that as it is the foundation for the future."
 24 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We don't think about records' published at 17:14 GMT 17:14 GMT 
 FT: Bournemouth 2-0 Nottm Forest 
 Bournemouth 
 Bournemouth manager Marco Rose speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "We don't think about records, we just think about the next game. We took the right approach. We knew it would be tough and we would have to stay patient, and that's what we did. It was a top performance and a deserved win."
 On Evanilson, who scored in the sixth straight league match: "The way he works for us out of possession, works as a link player and goes deep. The way he scores is quite impressive.
 On going fourth: "Tonight I will smile, but not just because of the table - because we win."

 Bruno's reception published at 17:13 GMT 17:13 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 Alex Howell 
BBC Sport football reporter at St James' Park 
 Bruno Guimaraes already received a pretty hostile welcome when he arrived at the ground and there were some boos as he came out to do the warm-up in the Arsenal colours. 
 The reception he gets will be a lot more noticeable once he comes out and the game gets underway. 
 The Newcastle supporters aren't pleased with the way he left the club.

 'Long road but we're ready for it' published at 17:11 GMT 17:11 GMT 
 Chelsea 1-4 Leeds 
 Leeds United 
 Leeds captain Ethan Ampadu: "People talk about turning points and we have to learn about stuff that didn't work and try to better that."
 On earning a first win at Chelsea since 1999: "We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance."
 On talk of being in contention for a European place: "We have to be realistic and understand how hard this league is. We need to back this up next week, if we don't then this performance is wasted. We know where we want to get Leeds back to. It could be a long road but we're ready for it."

 'He's such a talent' published at 17:08 GMT 17:08 GMT 
 FT: Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham goalscorer Dominic Solanke on 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett's performance: "Luca was magnificent today. We see him in training every day, we know what a player he is. he's such a talent, honestly. 
 "To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy. We'll be celebrating with him today. He can bring so much for us.
 "He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like. But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that. And he's obviously got that confidence about him which is great to have to play in the Premier League and play for a team like Tottenham.
 "We can see so much in him. It's exciting times for all of us, especially him."

Former England goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live at Stamford Bridge

 Stand out performance and a statement win. People will start to take note.

 'Arsenal will win comfortably' published at 17:01 GMT 17:01 GMT 
 Newcastle v Arsenal (17:30 GMT) 
 I am covering this game and I think it is a huge one for Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle.
 The Magpies have picked up as many points - 12 - in their first 10 games under Jaissle as they did when Eddie Howe was in charge last season, but I still don't think their fans are overly convinced by him.
 Some of their unease is because Newcastle don't seem to have a defined style of play, and can be a bit kamikaze going forward.
 Because of that, I just think Arsenal will pick them off, and win comfortably.
 The Gunners have conceded only five league goals so far and have made an incredible start to their title defence with nine wins out of 10.
 The worry for their rivals is that it feels to me Mikel Arteta's side have not even got going yet, but I still don't see anyone being close to them.
 Sutton's prediction: 0-2

 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Frustrated Aston Villa manager Unai Emery attempting to get the game going again against Sunderland at Villa Park
 By Phil McNulty Chief football writer at Villa Park Aston Villa's struggles at home this season continued as they were held to a goalless draw by Sunderland in a low-quality encounter. 
 Unai Emery's men have toiled at Villa Park this season, winning only one Premier League game out of five before facing the Black Cats - and it was a case of 'same again' as they were unable to gather any momentum for long periods.
 There were only brief flashes of attacking invention in the first half, when youngster Johan Manzambi brought a smart diving save from Robin Roefs, before Emiliano Buendia failed to punish a poor clearance from the Sunderland keeper.
 Sunderland were missing the threat of injured Brian Brobbey and the midfield influence of captain Granit Xhaka, but defended resolutely and with great organisation.
 Villa captain John McGinn, on as substitute after an hour, tried to find a spark, with manager Emery cutting an increasingly frustrated figure in his technical area.
 Ross Barkley, another Villa substitute, almost broke through when he brought a flying save from Roefs late on, the keeper also keeping out a header from his own defender Nordi Mukiele.
 Chemsdine Talbi then almost won it for Sunderland in stoppage time with a curling effort that was only inches wide.
 Aston Villa analysis: No home comfort for frustrated Emery 
 The sight of Barkley firing a last-ditch effort high into the Holte End before jeers rang around Villa Park at the final whistle seconds later summed up an afternoon of sheer frustration for Aston Villa and manager Emery.
 Whether it is the temporary surroundings of a three-sided Villa Park, or the inevitable period of transition after losing six of the starting line-up that won the Europa League against Freiburg in Istanbul in May, Emery's team were once again lacking punch and spark.
 It showed in Emery's increasingly animated touchline demeanour, especially when Villa failed to take advantage of inviting crosses into the box.
 This is early days in the revolution Emery has had to undertake after a summer of upheaval, but this was a very poor display which met with the disapproval of a large portion of supporters at its conclusion.
 Sunderland analysis: Black Cats' fight will delight Le Bris 
 Sunderland needed to build on the vital victory against Chelsea at the Stadium of Light in their last game, a first Premier League win since August, and they did so with a deserved point at Villa Park.
 This was a result built on resilience and the calm and highly competent goalkeeping of Roefs, especially as Sunderland were missing two such vital contributors in Brobbey and Xhaka.
 Villa had most of the chances, but Sunderland were resilient and never under any sustained pressure, while also containing a threat on the break.
 And it almost brought them victory in those closing moments but Talbi clutched his head in anguish as he watched his clever effort land inches wide, with Villa keeper Zion Suzuki well beaten.
 It was not to be, but this was still a creditable point for Sunderland and head coach Regis le Bris.
